newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suspected Egypt militants kill three in south.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Egypt militants kill three in south.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants on Tuesday killed a Coptic Christian farmer and two policemen in the southern Egyptian village of Taha al-Amedah, security sources said.
They said villagers stumbled on the body of farmer Kamal Estafanos, whose throat had been slit, and reported it to the police.

Gunmen believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) fighting to topple the government then shot at the investigating police, killing Sharhat Mohamed Qenawi and wounding seven other policemen chasing them in the wheat fields of Minya province some 240 miles (150 km) south of Cairo.
Police also found the body of policeman Helmy Mikhail, whom the suspected militants had slaughtered earlier in the fields surrounding his home.

The sources said the militants killed Estafanos because they thought he was a police informer. Copts and policemen have also been targets for the Gama'a, fighting since 1992 to transform Egypt into a purist Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed and scores wounded since the campaign began.
